title: Shard-key normalization and online migration plan for control-plane schema
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Background: Control plane queries for tenant-scoped metadata are exhibiting heavy hotspots on a single large table (control_entities). Historical FK churn, non-normalized shard keys, and broad indexes cause frequent full-index scans and MVCC bloat. This ticket defines a safe, online path to: 1) normalize shard key values used by routing (tenant_key -> tenant_id_hash), 2) introduce a partitioned/resharded table layout that reduces per-tenant scan amplification, 3) implement online, asynchronous record migration with a sync-trigger fallback, and 4) add targeted partial indexes and telemetry to avoid regressions. Goal: reduce p99 control-plane read latency by 40% for tenant-heavy workloads and decrease index bloat and vacuum churn by 30%.
acceptance_criteria: New normalized shard column tenant_id_hash exists and is populated for 100% of active rows via async backfill
control_entities has a partitioned sibling table control_entities_shard keyed on tenant_id_hash and time range
No locking maintenance window >5s for migration steps in production; all heavy work done with row-by-row background worker
Query plans for top-10 control-plane hotpaths show use of partial indexes; p99 read latency improvement >= 35% on staging
Rollback path documented and automated (trigger-based mirror until cutover)
technical_plan: Audit query patterns with pg_stat_statements and upsert common filter predicate sets
Add new computed column tenant_id_hash (sha1 or murmur3) and index it concurrently
Create partitioned table control_entities_shard PARTITION BY LIST (tenant_id_hash % 64) to reduce hot partitions
Implement an async migration worker (k8s job + idempotent SQL) that copies rows in small batches, marks source rows with migrated=true, and verifies checksums
Deploy a DB trigger + logical replication slot that mirrors writes to the shard table during migration window for zero-data-loss sync
Introduce partial indexes for active_time_range and status='active' to keep index size small for hot queries
Run pg_repack or reindex concurrently on original table to mitigate bloat before final cutover
Switch reads to control_entities_shard using a feature flag and observability gates; keep write-through to both tables until verification
Remove legacy FK constraints discovered as unused, after dependency sweep and QA
Post-cutover: decommission old table or keep as archive partition for 90 days depending on retention policy
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Long-running copy jobs might lag behind writes under high traffic. Mitigation: throttled workers, multi-worker parallelism by hash bucket, and a trigger-based mirror for final sync.
Risk: Index bloat increases temp I/O. Mitigation: schedule pg_repack on low-traffic windows and use max_live_workers limit.
Risk: ORM assumptions about primary keys or FK names break. Mitigation: compatibility layer in service code, dark-deploy schema changes, and a migration compatibility test-suite in CI.
Risk: Incorrect tenant normalization producing collisions. Mitigation: use 64-bit hash with collision detection step in backfill job and fall back to full tenant UUID when collision observed.
observability_and_testing: Add dedicated Dashboards: control-plane-top-queries, tenant-shard-imbalance (histogram by tenant_id_hash modulo), migration-lag (rows_left, throughput)
Add pg_stat_statements alert rule for N+1 or repeated full-index scans exceeding threshold
End-to-end staging load test with top-50 tenants replayed; measure p50/p95/p99 improvements and verify no dropped writes
Unit/Integration tests for migration worker (idempotency, resumability) and trigger mirror logic
Add post-migration QA runbooks and queries (row counts, checksums, latest_updated match)
Retention: keep audit logs of migration jobs and checksums in control_plane_migration_log table
runbook_steps: Step 0: Preflight - run schema diff and pre-checker script (links below)
Step 1: Deploy tenant_id_hash computed column and concurrent index
Step 2: Deploy migration worker to staging and run full backfill; validate checksums
Step 3: Create partitioned shards and start small-batch copy in production under throttle
Step 4: Enable trigger mirror; monitor migration-lag; iterate until rows_left < 0.1%
Step 5: Feature-flag switch reads to partitioned table; monitor error rates and latency for 24h
Step 6: Cutover writes if stable; disable trigger and schedule final repack of old table
Step 7: Post-cutover verification and cleanup (drop old indexes, remove unused FKs, archive table)
